tasks.title: Spike: Todoist filter query support matrix
acceptance: Document lists every filter-query construct the client may encounter (`today`, `overdue`, `#project`, `@label`, `p1`..`p4`, `no date`, `no labels`, `assigned to:`, `search:`, date ranges, `&` / `|` / `!` / parentheses) with a verdict per construct: `supported-locally` or `unsupported`
For each `supported-locally` construct the doc names the cached columns/queries (EPIC-04 read layer) needed to evaluate it, without referencing file paths that do not exist yet
Document states the fallback rule explicitly: any filter whose query contains at least one `unsupported` construct is rendered as 'server-defined / unsupported' and never evaluated partially
Document fixes the grammar subset to be implemented in T-902 (token kinds, operator precedence, parenthesis handling) in a short EBNF-style block
Document records at least 6 concrete example filter queries with the expected verdict for each, to be reused verbatim as test fixtures in T-903
No production code is changed by this task
tasks.context: The epic explicitly flags that the Todoist filter query language is rich and needs a spike before implementation. Follow the style of the existing notes in `docs/manual/` (e.g. `epic-03-sync-api.md`). Saved filters arrive from the Sync API as the `filters` resource already modelled in `src/api/model/filter.rs` - read it for the available fields (`query`, `name`, `is_deleted`, ordering). Decide conservatively: when in doubt, mark a construct unsupported.

tasks.title: Fuzzy matcher core: subsequence matching and ranking
acceptance: `src/search/fuzzy.rs` exposes `fn match_score(needle: &str, haystack: &str) -> Option<MatchScore>` returning `None` when the needle is not a case-insensitive subsequence of the haystack
`MatchScore` carries the numeric score plus the matched byte ranges so the UI can highlight them later
Scoring rewards contiguous runs, matches at word boundaries and prefix matches; ties are broken deterministically by shorter haystack then byte order, so ranking is stable for a fixed fixture set
Empty needle matches every haystack with a constant score; matching is Unicode-safe (no panics or byte-boundary slicing on multi-byte input, covered by a test with non-ASCII content)
`src/search/mod.rs` declares the module with module docs following the `src/api/mod.rs` pattern; `src/main.rs` declares `mod search;`
No `unwrap`/`expect` in non-test code; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Pure, dependency-free matching logic - no cache or UI access, so it can land before EPIC-04/EPIC-07 merge. Keep the crate dependency set unchanged (no new fuzzy crate): Cargo.lock pins must not move. Crate-wide `Result<T, AppError>` applies only to fallible functions; matching itself is infallible and returns `Option`.

tasks.title: Filter query parser for the supported grammar subset
acceptance: `src/filters/parse.rs` exposes `fn parse(query: &str) -> Result<FilterAst, Unsupported>` implementing exactly the grammar subset fixed in `docs/manual/epic-10-filter-support.md`
`FilterAst` models the boolean structure (`And`, `Or`, `Not`, parentheses) over leaf predicates (project, label, priority, date-relative, no-date, no-labels)
Any construct marked `unsupported` in the spike, any parse error, and any unknown token yield `Unsupported { reason: String }` - never a partially-parsed AST
`Unsupported` carries a short human-readable reason suitable for display in the UI (e.g. `unsupported: assigned to:`)
The 6+ example queries recorded in the spike are covered by unit tests asserting the exact supported/unsupported verdict
Operator precedence (`!` > `&` > `|`) and explicit parentheses are unit-tested against at least 3 nested examples
`src/main.rs` declares `mod filters;`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Parsing only - no evaluation and no cache access here, so this is unblocked by EPIC-04. Keep the parser hand-written (no new parser dependency). Follow the `thiserror` style used in `src/error.rs` for `Unsupported`; do not add a new variant to `AppError` unless the parser is actually called from a fallible app path (it is not yet).

tasks.title: Search over cached tasks with view scoping
acceptance: `src/search/query.rs` exposes `fn search(items: &[SearchItem], needle: &str, scope: SearchScope) -> Vec<SearchHit>` where `SearchScope` is `CurrentView { ids }` or `All`

`SearchItem` is a thin, cache-agnostic struct (`id`, `content`, `description`, `project_id`, optional `section_id`) built from the EPIC-04 read layer, so this module does not depend on rusqlite directly
A task that matches only in its `description` and not in its `content` is returned (explicit unit test)
When both fields match, the better of the two scores is used and the matched field is reported on `SearchHit` so the UI can show where the hit was
Results are sorted by descending score with the stable tie-break from T-902; the order is asserted against a fixed fixture of at least 10 items
`SearchScope::CurrentView` restricts results to the supplied id set; `SearchScope::All` ignores it (unit-tested both ways)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Depends on EPIC-04's cached-task read queries, which are planned in parallel and not merged yet - that is why the input is a borrowed `&[SearchItem]` slice the caller builds, not a DB handle. Keep it allocation-light: the perf test in T-908 runs this on 5k items per keystroke.

tasks.title: Local filter evaluation against cached tasks
acceptance: `src/filters/eval.rs` exposes `fn evaluate(ast: &FilterAst, items: &[FilterItem], today: NaiveDateLike) -> Vec<ItemId>` with the current date injected (no `now()` call inside), so tests are deterministic
`FilterItem` is a cache-agnostic struct carrying the fields the supported predicates need (project, labels, priority, due date, completed flag), mirroring the T-904 approach
Each supported leaf predicate from the spike has at least one positive and one negative unit test against a fixed fixture of tasks
Boolean composition (`&`, `|`, `!`, parentheses) is evaluated with the precedence asserted in T-903; at least 3 composite queries are unit-tested
`pub fn resolve(query: &str, ...) -> FilterResult` returns `FilterResult::Unsupported { reason }` when `parse` rejects the query, and never returns a partial result set
Deleted and completed items are excluded from results unless the query explicitly asks for them; asserted by test
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Pairs with the EPIC-04 cache reads (planned in parallel): the caller materialises `FilterItem`s from the cache and passes them in. Date-relative predicates (`today`, `overdue`) must use the injected date and the due/deadline shapes already modelled in `src/api/model/common.rs` - reuse those types rather than re-parsing date strings.

tasks.title: Search session state machine with escape/restore
acceptance: `src/search/state.rs` exposes `SearchSession` with `open(previous_view, previous_selection)`, `push_char`, `pop_char`, `set_scope`, `clear`, `cancel`, `accept`
`open` snapshots the caller's view identifier and selected task id; `cancel` returns that exact snapshot so the caller can restore the previous view and selection (unit-tested)
`clear` empties the query but keeps the session open with the original snapshot intact; `cancel` from an already-empty query still closes the session
`accept` returns the currently highlighted `SearchHit` (or `None` when there are no results) for jump-to-task
Results are recomputed incrementally on every query mutation via `search()` from T-904; the highlighted index is clamped into range after every recompute (unit-tested with a shrinking result set)
Scope toggling between current-view and all re-runs the query without losing the typed text (unit-tested)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: This is the headless half of the `/` search UX so that it is testable without a terminal; EPIC-07's app loop (planned in parallel) will own the key dispatch that drives it. Keep view/selection identifiers generic (e.g. a `ViewId` enum defined here or an opaque string) so wiring to EPIC-07's actual view type is a small adapter, not a rewrite.

tasks.title: TUI search prompt, incremental results list and jump-to-task
acceptance: Pressing `/` opens a one-line search prompt and the task list is replaced by the ranked results list, updating on every keystroke
Result rows show task content, parent project and an indicator when the hit came from the description only; matched ranges from T-902 are highlighted
`Esc` closes the prompt and restores the exact previous view and selected task (snapshot from T-906), asserted by a rendered-buffer snapshot test before/after
`Enter` jumps to the highlighted task: the underlying view switches to that task's project and the task becomes the selection
A key toggles search scope between current view and all, and the prompt renders the active scope
The scope-toggle and search keys are registered in the keymap so the `?` help overlay lists them with no hardcoded duplicate string (asserted by test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Depends on the EPIC-07 TUI shell, which is planned in parallel and not merged yet - the exact module names under `src/ui/` must follow whatever EPIC-07 lands; if they differ, stop and ask rather than inventing a parallel UI structure. EPIC-07 only binds `/` to open the prompt; all matching behaviour belongs here. Reuse EPIC-07's existing buffer-snapshot test helpers rather than adding new ones.

tasks.title: Search keystroke latency test at 5k cached items
acceptance: Test generates a deterministic synthetic fixture of 5000 `SearchItem`s (seeded, no network, no DB) with realistic content and description lengths
Test simulates typing a 6-character query one character at a time and measures each incremental `search()` call with `std::time::Instant`
Assertion: the p95 per-keystroke duration is below 16ms; the measured p50/p95/max are printed so CI logs show the margin
The threshold is applied only in release-equivalent conditions or with a documented debug-build multiplier, so the test is not flaky on CI debug builds
No new crate dependency is added (no criterion); `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` are unchanged
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: The epic's acceptance demands <16ms per keystroke at 5k items. Existing integration tests live in `tests/` (see `tests/sync_client.rs`) - follow their layout and the fixture conventions in `tests/fixtures/`. Use fake task content only; never real Todoist data.

tasks.title: Sidebar Filters section and read-only filter view
acceptance: Sidebar renders a `Filters` section listing the saved filters from the cache, ordered by the filter resource's order field, with deleted filters hidden
Selecting a filter renders its task set, evaluated locally via T-905 against cached items, in the normal task list layout
A filter whose query is `Unsupported` renders a clear 'server-defined filter - cannot be evaluated locally' message plus the reason, and shows no task rows (never a partial or wrong result set)

Filter view is read-only: every mutating key binding (add/edit/complete/delete/move/reorder/comment) is ignored while a filter view is focused and produces no command enqueue - asserted by a key-handling test that feeds each mutating key and checks no action is emitted
An empty filter result renders an explicit 'no matching tasks' empty state rather than a blank pane
Snapshot tests cover the three states: populated filter, empty filter, unsupported filter
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Depends on the EPIC-07 sidebar (planned in parallel; it reserves a Filters slot) and on the EPIC-04 cache reads for the `filters` resource modelled in `src/api/model/filter.rs`. Creating or editing filters is explicitly out of scope. If EPIC-07's final sidebar module name differs from `src/ui/sidebar.rs`, stop and ask.

tasks.title: Integration tests for search and filter views over a cache fixture
acceptance: Fixture seeds a cache with projects, labels, tasks (including one matching only in its description) and at least one supported and one unsupported saved filter - all fake data, no real ids or tokens
End-to-end-through-the-cache test: open search, type a query, assert the result set and ordering; assert the description-only task appears
Test: toggling scope from current view to all widens the result set for the same query
Test: `Esc` after a search restores the previous view and the previously selected task id
Test: `Enter` on a result switches the active view to that task's project with the task selected
Test: selecting the supported saved filter yields exactly the expected task ids from cache with no network call
Test: selecting the unsupported saved filter renders the unsupported indication and zero task rows
Test: each mutating key pressed in filter view leaves the write queue empty
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Follow the integration-test conventions already in `tests/` (`tests/sync_client.rs`, `tests/sync_fixture.rs`) and the JSON fixture style of `tests/fixtures/sync_full.json`. These tests sit on top of EPIC-04's cache and EPIC-07's app harness; use their test helpers rather than duplicating setup.

tasks.title: Document search and saved-filter behaviour
acceptance: Doc describes the `/` search UX: incremental matching, what fields are searched, scope toggle, Esc/Enter behaviour
Doc explains fuzzy ranking in user terms (subsequence, case-insensitive, contiguity and prefix bonuses) with 2-3 worked examples
Doc explains saved filters: read-only, locally evaluated, and links to the support matrix in `docs/manual/epic-10-filter-support.md` for which queries are unsupported and why
Doc states the measured keystroke-latency budget and where the test that enforces it lives
README gains a short Search & filters bullet in the feature list linking to the new doc
All key bindings mentioned match the keymap registered in T-907 (no drift); `cargo test --all` still passes
tasks.context: Match the tone and structure of the existing `docs/manual/epic-02-auth-checks.md` and `docs/manual/epic-03-sync-api.md`. Documentation only - no code changes.
